aix432.notes: Framebuffer console only: AIX's LFT draws through the emulated Matrox GXT130P. The pointer is PS/2 relative on the wire (no tablet on a 40p) but ABSOLUTE to the daemon: AIX drives the Matrox HARDWARE cursor, so QEMU reads the guest's own pointer position back out of the DAC CURPOSX/Y registers and a closed loop inside hw/display/mga.c converges on the commanded pixel -- labctl 'abs x y' lands 1:1 and nothing dead-reckons. Keys still ride the QEMU/dbus path. Exec is telnet_unix_e: AIX's own telnetd on the retronet tap at 10.99.0.28:23, dialled from labhost only -- the AIXRN-IN containment chain still blocks every guest-originated packet, so the guest gained no reach. Reset restores the in-qcow2 'golden' snapshot, which skips the genuine IBM firmware's POST entirely -- a cold boot walks that POST and takes 15-25 minutes.

Reset=relaunch: fresh work HDF reflinked from disk/amigaos35-system.hdf.golden + --load_state of sta/'Saved State 1.uss' + FS_UAE_MOUSEHACK_ADDR re-arm (the addr is PAIRED with the statefile). amix.notes: HOST-NATIVE: FS-UAE 3.2.35 (its OWN copy at assets/amix/fsuae-native, built with FSUAE_STATION=amix) runs an Amiga 3000 (68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04 r37.175) on the host inside a pinned Xvfb sized to the emulator window; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11) and injects input over XTEST. No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel. POINTER IS OPEN: the daemon injects absolute XTEST motion (the x11test contract), but the GUEST tracks it relatively and with acceleration — the UAE mousehack that gives amigaos35 a 1:1 pointer is an AmigaOS trap, and AMIX drives the Amiga mouse hardware itself. Measured on the sandbox rig: host (160,120)->guest ~(82,92), host (480,380)->guest ~(331,345), history-dependent. The tile stays hidden until this is closed (an x11test-rel daemon backend, or FS-UAE grab-mode calibration). Reset=relaunch: cold boot (~2 min) of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden; no statefile. Launcher stations/amix/x11-runtime.sh.

tru64.notes: x11 runtime (es40 AlphaServer ES40 emulator, headless SDL dummy + shm capture) — SRM-boots the disk directly, no ARC autoboot. No QMP; input = streamhost mamesock -> es40 ctlsock mamectl/1 unix socket ctl.sock. es40 binary is multi-client ctlsock (operator tools can inject input beside the attached daemon). Serial pair 21974/21975 is this tile's claim; ser1 doubles as the EXEC channel — exec_kind serialcon_e: the guest runs a getty on /dev/tty01 and the tile's pumps.py lends that line one client at a time over serial-exec.sock in the tile dir, so `labctl exec tru64 <cmd>` returns captured stdout and the guest's exit code with no network device in the machine. Pointer is ABSOLUTE and pixel-exact: the launcher sets ES40_POINTER_GAIN=2 because this guest moves 2 px per injected PS/2 count (odd targets land 1 px short), and the checkpoint carries X acceleration 1/1 threshold 0. Screen is 1280x1024 via -screen on the X server line in /etc/dt/config/Xservers. reset = relaunch restoring the CHECKPOINT: the launcher reflink-copies assets/tru64/checkpoint/tru64.img and restores checkpoint/tru64.axp (ES40_RESTORE), CDE desktop ~3 s after exec instead of the ~7-10 min cold boot; rollback = delete assets/tru64/checkpoint/ and it cold-boots img/tru64-seed.img.

The agent is C:\WARPNET.EXE (streamhost/guest-agents/win9x/warpnet.c built -DWARP_PORT=7788), binding 0.0.0.0:7788; reached DIRECTLY over the retronet bridge at the guest IP 10.99.0.10:7788 (n0 is a tap on vmbr-rn, NOT slirp — no hostfwd). It is RUNNING inside the golden and restarts from the StartUp folder on a cold boot. No stderr (COMMAND.COM has no 2>&1). NEVER launch a full-screen DOS box: it wedges the display driver until loadvm golden. See docs/lab/retronet/ICQ-STATION.md, EXEC-CHANNEL.md

winxp.notes: no exec channel: use 'labctl sh' (blind) or clone (solaris clone has ssh) for real exec
